speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned right groin pain and abnormal leg positioning after a rear-end collision; can you describe exactly how your leg is positioned now and when the pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details. The mechanism of injury and immediate onset of severe right groin pain are concerning for an acetabular fracture or hip dislocation. Given the abnormal positioning of your leg, can you specifically describe whether your right hip is held in a flexed, abducted, and externally rotated position, or if it appears shortened and externally rotated?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Posterior Hip Dislocation. The mechanism of injury (rear-end collision) combined with the specific presentation of a shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated leg is pathognomonic for this condition. Please confirm if you can feel the femoral head palpating anteriorly in the groin, and I will prepare imaging immediately.
